$comment: Cross-SDK LITE filtering conformance corpus. BOTH the Node and Python SDKs execute these exact vectors (node/tests/filterParityCorpus.test.ts, python/tests/test_filter_parity_corpus.py) through their public `wrap()` API and must produce identical `data` plus the same SET of `filtered_keys` (order-independent; Node returns encounter order, Python sorted). A divergence here means the two SDKs protect data differently for the same input — a cross-SDK security-parity regression — and fails CI. This is the drift-proof foundation that hand-mirrored per-SDK tests cannot guarantee. Inputs are plain JSON (no ORM/Pydantic shapes) so the corpus is language-neutral.

cases.doc: scope keeps only listed top-level keys; everything else removed
explicit scope:[] is a maximally-restrictive whitelist (fail-closed)
deny_fields removes listed keys, keeps the rest
dot-notation keeps a nested field, drops its siblings
dot-notation deny removes only the nested field
dot-notation scope filters each element of a list-of-dicts
fail-closed: a bare leaf scope over a list-of-dicts drops the whole key
fail-closed: a bare leaf scope over a nested object drops the whole key
fail-closed: a nested scope path over a scalar value drops the key
S017 H1: deny_fields=['card.cvv'] removes a top-level key LITERALLY named 'card.cvv' (flattened-key API), not only a nested card->cvv. Was fail-OPEN (leaked).
S017 H1: deny_fields=['profile'] also drops a flattened 'profile.ssn' child key (everything under a denied node).
S017 H8/H9: an explicitly-scoped '__proto__' key is kept as ordinary data (parity: Python keeps it; Node must store it as an own property, not the prototype).
S017 H8/H9: an out-of-scope '__proto__' key is removed AND reported in filtered_keys (Node previously under-reported it = silent audit gap).
a bare leaf over a record nested one collection deeper ([[{...}]]) drops the key, as over [{...}]: checking only the immediate elements let the nested record through unfiltered and unreported
the same at three levels: the depth of the nesting does not matter
